account:
Today there seems to be a coordinated gathering behind the ordinary town business. My morning grain inspection went well, and the secretary says there are no council letters or outstanding office matters. Yet several people have been preparing something in the town hall. The builder specifically asked that the great hall door remain closed until eighteen, when my approved appointment calls for a lighting inspection. That door is still closed. The builder, freight, innkeeper, neighbour and secretary are now gathered nearby with me.

There is food involved: I heard a towns-person report that the innkeeper carried a sack of bread to the town hall. At tea, neighbour told me they had been asking neighbours for bread or grain donations for a community supper. Builder has also mentioned a service acknowledgement. When I asked neighbour whose service was being recognised and who organised it, neighbour said builder had asked them to bring me and left the details for the organisers to explain. Neighbour is here to walk into the hall with me, and secretary will accompany us too.

My suspicion is that the lighting inspection provides an occasion for a community supper and some sort of planned acknowledgement, perhaps a surprise thanking me for my service. The escort, closed hall, preparations and reluctance to explain would fit that. But nobody has actually told me who is being honoured, and I have not seen inside the hall, so that remains a guess rather than something I know. I intend to keep the eighteen o'clock appointment and find out without opening the hall early.
